title: Do Election Outcomes Matter for Life Satisfaction?
abstract: Abstract: Prior research suggests declines in life satisfaction among supporters of losing parties, but evidence largely stems from two-party systems. Drawing on goal-regulation and social-identity perspectives, we examined election-related changes in global and domain-specific life satisfaction in a multiparty system across the East German state elections 2024 ( N = 1,211) and the federal election in Germany 2025 ( N = 301), considering objective and subjective indicators of electoral success and vote choice. Across studies, these indicators were largely unrelated to changes in life satisfaction, with only isolated effects among AfD and BSW voters. Overall, even amid substantial political change, collective political outcomes had limited consequences for life satisfaction up to three months later, highlighting the limits of simple winner–loser accounts in multiparty contexts.
